<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-organic-tomatoes-free-from-heavy-metals" data-anchor="are-organic-tomatoes-free-from-heavy-metals" data-question="Are organic tomatoes free from heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are organic tomatoes free from heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No. Organic-labelled tomatoes in Americas monitoring data had a detected lead median of 1.7 µg/kg and cadmium of 8.2 µg/kg, close to unlabelled tomatoes.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Organically grown Polish tomatoes measured on a dry-weight basis held 26–139 µg/kg lead and 71–216 µg/kg cadmium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/grochowska-niedworok2020-cadmium-lead-tomatoes-poland|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Grochowska-Niedworok E, Nieć J, Baranowska R · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/grochowska-niedworok2020-cadmium-lead-tomatoes-poland">Assessment of cadmium and lead content in tomatoes and tomato products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Roczniki Państwowego Zakładu Higieny (Annals of the National Institute of Hygiene)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/grochowska-niedworok2020-cadmium-lead-tomatoes-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-tomato-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-tomato-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of tomato have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of tomato have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one Romanian survey, red cherry tomatoes held 18.6 µg/kg lead and no detectable cadmium against 66.8 µg/kg lead and 16.5 µg/kg cadmium in standard tomatoes.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bora FD, Bunea A, Pop SR, Banita SI, Dusa DS, Chira A, Bunea CI · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Quantification and Reduction in Heavy Metal Residues in Some Fruits and Vegetables: A Case Study Galați County, Romania</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Horticulturae</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Their arsenic was similar, and no other study compared types under one method, so this is a single observation.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bora FD, Bunea A, Pop SR, Banita SI, Dusa DS, Chira A, Bunea CI · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Quantification and Reduction in Heavy Metal Residues in Some Fruits and Vegetables: A Case Study Galați County, Romania</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Horticulturae</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-growing-regions-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-growing-regions-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which growing regions have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which growing regions have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

United States market baskets were lowest for lead (all below 4 µg/kg) and among the lowest for cadmium (median 3.3 µg/kg), and Polish and western Iranian surveys found fresh-weight cadmium means of 3 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/heshmati2020-iran-vegetables-cereals-pb-cd|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ali Heshmati, Fereshteh Mehri, Javad Karami-Momtaz, Amin Mousavi Khaneghah · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/heshmati2020-iran-vegetables-cereals-pb-cd">Concentration and Risk Assessment of Potentially Toxic Elements, Lead and Cadmium, in Vegetables and Cereals Consumed in Western Iran</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Protection 83(1):101-107</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/heshmati2020-iran-vegetables-cereals-pb-cd">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> These are purchase markets or single surveys; the evidence supports avoiding exposed sites more than choosing a country.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li R, Wu H, Ding J, Fu W, Gan L, Li Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Mercury pollution in vegetables, grains and soils from areas surrounding coal-fired power plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ahmed2023-trace-metals-tomato-wastewater|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahmed A, Hassan I, Abd-Elrahman S, ElSayed M · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ahmed2023-trace-metals-tomato-wastewater">Trace metal concentrations in tomato fruits irrigated with industrial wastewater in Cairo and health risk assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ahmed2023-trace-metals-tomato-wastewater">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-tomato-products-contain-more-heavy-metals-than-fresh-tomatoes" data-anchor="do-tomato-products-contain-more-heavy-metals-than-fresh-tomatoes" data-question="Do tomato products contain more heavy metals than fresh tomatoes?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do tomato products contain more heavy metals than fresh tomatoes?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

They are different foods: concentration removes water, and canned products can take up tin from the can during storage.<sup class="cite">[[sources/buculei2012-tin-iron-migration-canned-food-romania|33]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Buculei A, Gutt G, Amariei S, Dabija A, Constantinescu G · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/buculei2012-tin-iron-migration-canned-food-romania">Study regarding the tin and iron migration from metallic cans into foodstuff during storage</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Agroalimentary Processes and Technologies, 18(4), 299-303</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/buculei2012-tin-iron-migration-canned-food-romania">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/trandafir2012-tin-canned-foods-icp-ms|34]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Trandafir I, Nour V, Ionica ME · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/trandafir2012-tin-canned-foods-icp-ms">Determination of Tin in Canned Foods by Inductively Coupled Plasma-Mass Spectrometry</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Polish Journal of Environmental Studies</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/trandafir2012-tin-canned-foods-icp-ms">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Their results are on the canned tomato, tomato paste and tomato sauce pages rather than on this page.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-do-the-levels-in-tomatoes-mean-for-health" data-anchor="what-do-the-levels-in-tomatoes-mean-for-health" data-question="What do the levels in tomatoes mean for health?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What do the levels in tomatoes mean for health?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Tomato is eaten in large amounts, so it contributes to intake even at low concentrations; it supplied 16% of estimated cadmium intake in Ismailia, Egypt, but 2–3% together with eggplant and okra in Australia.<sup class="cite">[[sources/loutfy2012-ismailia-foodstuffs-metals|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Loutfy N, Mentler A, Shoeab M, Ahmed MT, Fuerhacker M · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/loutfy2012-ismailia-foodstuffs-metals">Analysis and exposure assessment of some heavy metals in foodstuffs from Ismailia city, Egypt</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxicological &amp; Environmental Chemistry</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/loutfy2012-ismailia-foodstuffs-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study|39]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Food Standards Australia New Zealand · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study">25th Australian Total Diet Study</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Standards Australia New Zealand</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fsanz2019-25th-australian-total-diet-study">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Measured concentrations are not a safety verdict for any individual diet.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-tomatoes" data-anchor="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-tomatoes" data-question="Are there legal limits for heavy metals in tomatoes?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are there legal limits for heavy metals in tomatoes?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes. The EU limits fruiting vegetables, the food group in which EFSA classifies tomatoes, to 50 µg/kg lead and 20 µg/kg cadmium on a fresh-weight basis after washing, and to 400 µg/kg nickel from July 2025.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|29]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels|31]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 of 30 July 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as regards maximum levels of nickel in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union, L series, 2024/1987 (31.7.2024)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Codex sets 50 µg/kg lead for fruiting vegetables in its 2025 edition, and its cadmium maximum for fruiting vegetables does not apply to tomatoes.<sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-washing-tomatoes-remove-heavy-metals" data-anchor="does-washing-tomatoes-remove-heavy-metals" data-question="Does washing tomatoes remove heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does washing tomatoes remove heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Partly. In a Romanian study, soaking tap-washed tomatoes in 5% vinegar lowered total arsenic by about half, cadmium by 26–61% and lead by 19–24%.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bora FD, Bunea A, Pop SR, Banita SI, Dusa DS, Chira A, Bunea CI · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Quantification and Reduction in Heavy Metal Residues in Some Fruits and Vegetables: A Case Study Galați County, Romania</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Horticulturae</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metal taken up into the fruit is not removed by washing.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-cooking-destroy-heavy-metals-in-tomatoes" data-anchor="does-cooking-destroy-heavy-metals-in-tomatoes" data-question="Does cooking destroy heavy metals in tomatoes?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does cooking destroy heavy metals in tomatoes?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No. Boiling did not lower arsenic per gram of dry matter in tomatoes from arsenic-spiked irrigation.<sup class="cite">[[sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina|26]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clair-Caliot G, Marks SJ, Hug SJ, Bretzler A, N&#39;guessan ND, Tihe SFK, Lalanne F · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Uptake of Arsenic by Irrigated Vegetables and Cooked Food Products in Burkina Faso</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Water</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Cookware can add metals: foil baking raised aluminium from 80 to 370 µg/kg, and new stainless steel raised nickel and chromium in simmered tomato sauce.<sup class="cite">[[sources/hobbie2014-stainless-steel-ni-cr-leaching|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Hobbie KA, Kamerud KL, Anderson KA · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/hobbie2014-stainless-steel-ni-cr-leaching">Stainless Steel Leaches Nickel and Chromium into Foods During Cooking</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Society of Toxicology 2014 Annual Meeting (poster)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/hobbie2014-stainless-steel-ni-cr-leaching">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/dordevic2019-aluminum-foil-culinary-baking-czech|32]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dordevic D, Buchtova H, Jancikova S, Macharackova B, Jarosova M, Vitez T, Kushkevych I · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dordevic2019-aluminum-foil-culinary-baking-czech">Aluminum contamination of food during culinary preparation: Case study with aluminum foil and consumers&#39; preferences</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science &amp; Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dordevic2019-aluminum-foil-culinary-baking-czech">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-the-arsenic-in-tomatoes-the-more-toxic-inorganic-form" data-anchor="is-the-arsenic-in-tomatoes-the-more-toxic-inorganic-form" data-question="Is the arsenic in tomatoes the more toxic inorganic form?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is the arsenic in tomatoes the more toxic inorganic form?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Few results separate the forms: 11 of 38 European GEMS/Food inorganic arsenic results were detected, at up to 38.8 µg/kg, four Hong Kong composites were below 3 µg/kg, and EFSA estimated a mean of 1.5–7.7 µg/kg across 484 European results.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|29]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic|30]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Inorganic Arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Most studies measured total arsenic only.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bora FD, Bunea A, Pop SR, Banita SI, Dusa DS, Chira A, Bunea CI · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Quantification and Reduction in Heavy Metal Residues in Some Fruits and Vegetables: A Case Study Galați County, Romania</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Horticulturae</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-irrigating-tomatoes-with-wastewater-raise-heavy-metals" data-anchor="does-irrigating-tomatoes-with-wastewater-raise-heavy-metals" data-question="Does irrigating tomatoes with wastewater raise heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does irrigating tomatoes with wastewater raise heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies that compared it, yes for chromium, nickel and cadmium: Nile-irrigated Cairo fruit held 290 µg/kg chromium and 610 µg/kg nickel against 760 and 1,630 µg/kg with industrial wastewater.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ahmed2023-trace-metals-tomato-wastewater|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ahmed A, Hassan I, Abd-Elrahman S, ElSayed M · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ahmed2023-trace-metals-tomato-wastewater">Trace metal concentrations in tomato fruits irrigated with industrial wastewater in Cairo and health risk assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ahmed2023-trace-metals-tomato-wastewater">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Half reclaimed water in a Chinese trial raised cadmium from 18 to 29 µg/kg and chromium from 49 to 61 µg/kg, smaller differences that were not clearly significant.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2015-reclaimed-water-through-field-trials-on-the-content|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2015-reclaimed-water-through-field-trials-on-the-content">reclaimed water through field trials on the content and distribution of heavy metals in both tomatoes</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2015-reclaimed-water-through-field-trials-on-the-content">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-hydroponic-tomatoes-lower-in-heavy-metals" data-anchor="are-hydroponic-tomatoes-lower-in-heavy-metals" data-question="Are hydroponic tomatoes lower in heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are hydroponic tomatoes lower in heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one Shanghai study, yes: hydroponic tomatoes held 5.6 µg/kg lead and cadmium combined against 47.9 µg/kg for soil-grown tomatoes.<sup class="cite">[[sources/chen2024-shanghai-hydroponic-vegetables|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shanshan Chen, Chunxia Yao, Jiaxin Zhou, Haiyao Ma, Jing Jin, Weiguo Song, Zhenpeng Kai · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chen2024-shanghai-hydroponic-vegetables">Occurrence and Risk Assessment of Pesticides, Phthalates, and Heavy Metal Residues in Vegetables from Hydroponic and Conventional Cultivation</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 13, 1151</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chen2024-shanghai-hydroponic-vegetables">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Its nutrient water still carried lead (0.036 mg/L), so the result depends on clean water.<sup class="cite">[[sources/chen2024-shanghai-hydroponic-vegetables|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shanshan Chen, Chunxia Yao, Jiaxin Zhou, Haiyao Ma, Jing Jin, Weiguo Song, Zhenpeng Kai · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chen2024-shanghai-hydroponic-vegetables">Occurrence and Risk Assessment of Pesticides, Phthalates, and Heavy Metal Residues in Vegetables from Hydroponic and Conventional Cultivation</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods 13, 1151</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chen2024-shanghai-hydroponic-vegetables">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-tomatoes-grown-near-power-plants-or-mines-contain-more-metals" data-anchor="do-tomatoes-grown-near-power-plants-or-mines-contain-more-metals" data-question="Do tomatoes grown near power plants or mines contain more metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do tomatoes grown near power plants or mines contain more metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Near Chinese coal-fired power plants, tomato mercury reached 71.8–76.3 µg/kg at the closest sites against 0.73 µg/kg in a grocery-store sample.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li R, Wu H, Ding J, Fu W, Gan L, Li Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Mercury pollution in vegetables, grains and soils from areas surrounding coal-fired power plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In Seville, tomatoes from gardens in a mining district held less lead than city-garden tomatoes (89 against 165 µg/kg dry weight).<sup class="cite">[[sources/rossini-oliva2024-urban-garden-vegetables-spain|24]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rossini-Oliva S, López Nuñez R · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rossini-oliva2024-urban-garden-vegetables-spain">Is it healthy urban agriculture? Human exposure to potentially toxic elements in urban gardens from Andalusia, Spain</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rossini-oliva2024-urban-garden-vegetables-spain">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="why-are-some-reported-tomato-values-so-much-higher-than-others" data-anchor="why-are-some-reported-tomato-values-so-much-higher-than-others" data-question="Why are some reported tomato values so much higher than others?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Why are some reported tomato values so much higher than others?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Dry-weight results are about 17 times the fresh-weight concentration, and several papers report values that conflict with their own methods.<sup class="cite">[[sources/heshmati2020-iran-vegetables-cereals-pb-cd|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ali Heshmati, Fereshteh Mehri, Javad Karami-Momtaz, Amin Mousavi Khaneghah · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/heshmati2020-iran-vegetables-cereals-pb-cd">Concentration and Risk Assessment of Potentially Toxic Elements, Lead and Cadmium, in Vegetables and Cereals Consumed in Western Iran</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Protection 83(1):101-107</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/heshmati2020-iran-vegetables-cereals-pb-cd">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/jaishree2015-effluent-irrigated-crops-metals|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Jaishree, Khan TI · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jaishree2015-effluent-irrigated-crops-metals">Heavy metal accumulation in vegetables irrigated with industrial effluent</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Innovative Research in Science, Engineering and Technology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jaishree2015-effluent-irrigated-crops-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2025-detection-of-heavy-metals-concentration-in-vegetables-and|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2025-detection-of-heavy-metals-concentration-in-vegetables-and">Detection of heavy metals concentration in vegetables and</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2025-detection-of-heavy-metals-concentration-in-vegetables-and">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> This page shows those values with the reason and does not compare them.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="can-cooking-tomatoes-in-aluminium-or-stainless-steel-add-metals" data-anchor="can-cooking-tomatoes-in-aluminium-or-stainless-steel-add-metals" data-question="Can cooking tomatoes in aluminium or stainless steel add metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Can cooking tomatoes in aluminium or stainless steel add metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes. Baking tomato in foil raised aluminium about four-fold, and acidic tomato and meat dishes leached more aluminium from foil as acidity rose.<sup class="cite">[[sources/dordevic2019-aluminum-foil-culinary-baking-czech|32]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dordevic D, Buchtova H, Jancikova S, Macharackova B, Jarosova M, Vitez T, Kushkevych I · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dordevic2019-aluminum-foil-culinary-baking-czech">Aluminum contamination of food during culinary preparation: Case study with aluminum foil and consumers&#39; preferences</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science &amp; Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dordevic2019-aluminum-foil-culinary-baking-czech">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bassioni2012-aluminum-foil-meat-cooking-uae|35]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bassioni G, Mohammed FS, Al Zubaidy E, Kobrsi I · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bassioni2012-aluminum-foil-meat-cooking-uae">Risk Assessment of Using Aluminum Foil in Food Preparation</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Electrochemical Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bassioni2012-aluminum-foil-meat-cooking-uae">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Simmering tomato sauce with new stainless steel raised nickel and chromium sharply, an effect that faded after several cooking cycles.<sup class="cite">[[sources/hobbie2014-stainless-steel-ni-cr-leaching|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Hobbie KA, Kamerud KL, Anderson KA · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/hobbie2014-stainless-steel-ni-cr-leaching">Stainless Steel Leaches Nickel and Chromium into Foods During Cooking</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Society of Toxicology 2014 Annual Meeting (poster)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/hobbie2014-stainless-steel-ni-cr-leaching">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-there-aluminium-in-fresh-tomatoes" data-anchor="is-there-aluminium-in-fresh-tomatoes" data-question="Is there aluminium in fresh tomatoes?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is there aluminium in fresh tomatoes?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Fresh Czech tomatoes held 80 µg/kg aluminium before cooking, about 1,700 µg/kg on a dry-weight basis.<sup class="cite">[[sources/dordevic2019-aluminum-foil-culinary-baking-czech|32]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dordevic D, Buchtova H, Jancikova S, Macharackova B, Jarosova M, Vitez T, Kushkevych I · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dordevic2019-aluminum-foil-culinary-baking-czech">Aluminum contamination of food during culinary preparation: Case study with aluminum foil and consumers&#39; preferences</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Science &amp; Nutrition</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dordevic2019-aluminum-foil-culinary-baking-czech">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Aluminium is not limited in fresh vegetables by the EU or Codex instruments verified here.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels|31]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 of 30 July 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as regards maximum levels of nickel in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union, L series, 2024/1987 (31.7.2024)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
